identity.name: Yong (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Yong, one of the Three Qins

land.text: the Qin heartland west of Xianyang: 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

predecessors.note: One of the Three Qins with sai and zhai, given by Xiang Yu to the Qin general Zhang Han in the 206 BC division. Cliopatria's Yong row begins in 206.

land.text: Zhang Han's kingdom, taken by Liu Bang: 'Defeated by Liu Bang' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

successors.note: Feiqiu, Zhang Han's last stronghold, was flooded in June or July 205 BC (Zhang Han page); the kingdom-of-han dossier (ea-01) gains Yong in 205.

capitals.name: Feiqiu (Xingping)
capitals.note: Zhang Han page: 'Zhang Han retreated to Feiqiu (廢丘; present-day Xingping, Shaanxi) and remained there.' The page does not say he was crowned there; Feiqiu is the only seat any page opened names.

correction.text: unchanged, 206-205 BC; the table's 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu'

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (61,876 km2; 293 grid cells, 253 in Shaanxi, 23 in Gansu, 12 in Shanxi): it fits the table's 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu' and contains Feiqiu (Xingping) and Xianyang. The years change: the kingdom lasted 206-205, not to 204 (Zhang Han died in June or July 205). No page gives an area to compare.

region.text: the Kingdom of Yong: 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu' (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Zhang Han's kingdom in the Guanzhong heartland

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Zhang Han King of Yong. The Eighteen Kingdoms were 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'; the table has Yong, Zhang Han (Qin general), 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu'; the Zhang Han page: 'Zhang Han and his two deputies were made the rulers of three of the Eighteen Kingdoms' (tenure 206-205). 'Yong, Sai and Di were collectively known as the Three Qins because they occupied the area of the former Qin state.'

region.text: Zhang Han's kingdom in Guanzhong, invaded by Liu Bang in 206 BC

ledger.note: 206: Liu Bang attacks the Three Qins. Zhang Han page: Liu Bang's forces 'invaded Guanzhong and captured Zhang Han's kingdom in a surprise attack' later in 206 BC, leaving Zhang Han holding Feiqiu. The Chu-Han Contention page gives no year for the Chencang route and dates the conquest of the Three Qins 205 (Han Xin 'defeated the hastily regrouped Zhang Han, the King of Yong, in two consecutive battles'). Zone: the whole kingdom, contested from the invasion until Feiqiu falls.

region.text: Feiqiu and the rest of Zhang Han's kingdom

ledger.note: 205: Feiqiu is flooded and Zhang Han dies. 'A year later, in June or July 205 BC, the Han army flooded Feiqiu'; he 'committed suicide after his defeat, in June or July 205 BC, at Feiqiu (Xingping)'. The Chu-Han Contention page: 'Shortly after [the July-August 205 entry], Han forces conquered Feiqiu.'

region.text: 'central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu', Zhang Han's kingdom

ledger.note: 205: Yong passes to Liu Bang. Zhang Han page: tenure '206-205 BC', death 'June or July 205 BC, Xingping, Shaanxi'. Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Defeated by Liu Bang'. The kingdom-of-han dossier gains Yong in 205 (central Shaanxi and eastern Gansu). The page is silent on what Liu Bang did with the land afterwards (Longxi, Beidi, Shang commanderies are not mentioned).

region.text: Zhang Han's kingdom, 'Defeated by Liu Bang'

ledger.note: 205: the Kingdom of Yong ends with Zhang Han's death at Feiqiu (June or July 205 BC).

wars.name: Liu Bang's conquest of the Three Qins

zones.text: Zhang Han's kingdom in Guanzhong, held at Feiqiu until it was flooded

wars.outcome: Liu Bang's forces captured Zhang Han's kingdom in a surprise attack in 206 BC; Feiqiu held out until the Han army flooded it in June or July 205 and Zhang Han killed himself.
wars.note: The Chu-Han Contention page dates 'conquering the Three Qins in the Guanzhong region' to 205 and the surrender of Sima Xin, Dong Yi and Shen Yang to 205; the Sima Xin page dates their surrender 206.

certainty.note: The pages give provinces ('central Shaanxi, and eastern Gansu'), never a boundary; no treaty or survey line exists for a kingdom of one year.

sources.title: Eighteen Kingdoms
sources.note: The table of the eighteen kingdoms: Yong, Sai, Di, Yin and the others, with kings and modern territories; created by Xiang Yu in 206 BC; no capitals, no dates of fate.

sources.title: Zhang Han (Qin dynasty)
sources.note: King of Yong 206-205 BC, Feiqiu (Xingping), flooded June or July 205, suicide. (The page Zhang_Han is a disambiguation page and held nothing.)

sources.title: Chu-Han Contention
sources.note: Dated 205 BC for the conquest of the Three Qins, the surrender of Sima Xin, Dong Yi and Shen Yang, the attack on Henei in April-May 205, Feiqiu July-August 205.

notes: Cliopatria's Yong row (206-204) is cut to 206-205: Zhang Han died in June or July 205 (Zhang Han page) and the Chu-Han Contention page has the Three Qins conquered in 205. Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve Cliopatria rows; each row is its own kingdom (ea-02-b reached the same conclusion), so no merge. Pages opened: Eighteen Kingdoms, Zhang Han (Qin dynasty), Chu-Han Contention (3 against a budget of 1-2; the third settles the 205/206 conflict shared with sai and yin). The page 'Zhang Han' is a disambiguation page and held nothing. Not on any page: the partition of Guanzhong among Yong (west of Xianyang), Sai and Zhai, and what Liu Bang did with the land after 205; Longxi, Beidi and Shang commanderies are not named on the pages opened. No infobox area exists to compare with Cliopatria's 61,876 km2. Feiqiu is a page-based capital (Xingping); Zhang Han's coronation seat is not stated.
